items.title: Audible's new features let you explore book worlds — and use AI to talk to characters
items.excerpt: Audible is rolling out features that track characters, surface places and imagery mentioned in books, and let listeners interact with characters via generative AI.

items.title: Innovation with AI Abounds: The International Digital Publishing Award Announces 12 Finalists
items.excerpt: The International Digital Publishing Award names 12 finalists dominated by AI projects (AI translation, audiobooks, dyslexia tools); winners announced at Frankfurter Buchmesse next week.

items.title: AI narration companies are the audiobook industry's Trojan horse
items.excerpt: Audio specialist Jessica Barnfield argues AI voice firms like ElevenLabs aren't widening access to audiobooks so much as gathering publishers' data.

items.title: AI might kill us, but is that so bad?
items.excerpt: Novelist Bonnie Garmus argues that while AI has alarmed most writers, it has also exposed the hubris of humankind. Opinion column.

items.title: Opus 5.5 loves to tell you 'this matters' (and other AI writing tells)
items.excerpt: An analysis of model-specific prose tells finds Opus 5.5's biggest giveaway is the word 'dependable', used 23x more often than in human writing samples.

items.title: As AI-Generated Books Flood Amazon, Lynote's AI Detector And Note Generator Give Readers Two Different Kinds Of Control
items.excerpt: Citing data that AI-assisted titles now make up as much as 31% of new Amazon Top 25 entrants, the piece pitches Lynote's sentence-level AI detector for checking 'Look Inside' previews. Possibly advertorial; verify before picking.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Must-See Events
items.excerpt: PW's pre-fair guide: AI narration (Blinkist, Storytel), 'AI in Culture: Truth or Fiction?', AI and book publishing breakthroughs, and protecting content from AI text-and-data mining top Frankfurt's programme. Overlaps 09-25 Hall 4.1 card; push down.

items.title: Is AI coming for audiobooks?
items.excerpt: AI companies like ElevenLabs and Spoken are angling for the fast-growing audiobook market; it remains to be seen whether listeners will buy AI-narrated books.

items.title: Authors say AI-generated books are making human work harder to find
items.excerpt: Ohio authors raise concerns about AI-generated books crowding Amazon and about training data, saying the technology makes human work harder to discover.

items.title: Moon Over Lotus Isle: AI-co-created poem by Macao poet Ng Iat-i
items.excerpt: At the Mandarin's House, a UNESCO World Heritage site, Macao poet Ng Iat-i recites 'Moon Over Lotus Isle', a poem co-created with AI. Short video feature.

items.title: CharaLab Releases AI Manga Generator to Help Publisher Creating Manga & Comics Faster
items.excerpt: CharaLab launches an AI manga generator producing 1–6 panel pages in multiple art styles, pitched at publishers and creators for faster manga and comics production. Press release.

items.title: Publishers Hit the AI Jackpot
items.excerpt: Publishers stand to gain the most from Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement, and many writers aren't happy about it. Settlement-allocation follow-up; push down.

items.title: Stop asking writers if they used AI. Just ask them how much
items.excerpt: Jack Brewster proposes a 0–5 disclosure scale for how much AI went into a piece of writing, and labels his own column 'H3 Polished'.

items.title: Korean Manhwa Apocalypse: Hidden Risks Behind Chinese AI Comic Dramas' Global Expansion
items.excerpt: As Korean manhwa's overseas boom fades, Chinese AI-generated comic dramas are scaling globally, posing hidden risks to the webcomic business. Date from embedded publishTime.

items.title: Who is the storyteller in the age of AI?
items.excerpt: Op-ed tracing storytelling from Homer's epics to AI, arguing the medium changes while the search for meaning stays. Weak; filler only.
